_comment: Plane-4 standing tool-surface baseline (scripts/check-tool-surface.mjs). Growth is ALLOWED but never silent: raise a value and record `reason` + `recordedAt` saying what capability it buys. Dispatch-time caps are governed elsewhere and are not the subject of this baseline.

registry.toolDefinitions.reason: BI-B14253CD restores explicit initial platform funding ownership through read_platform_funding_setup and confirm_platform_funding_owner in the existing portfolio-budget pack. get_investment_balance requires an existing owner and cannot safely preview prospective ownership; allocation setters and funding binders must not infer or establish the platform policy owner. One bounded read contract and one exact-state human authority writer are separately discoverable, share the portal service, and reuse admin_read/admin_write without a new grant, core-tier entry or provider. Claim to check: a read writes nothing; current human, coworker, token and room restrictions intersect; missing human approval, changed state, partial or existing ownership and a copied-install repeat cannot write; an exact completed repeat performs no second mutation; ownership and audit commit together while allocations, history and policy ratification remain unchanged. The prior 462-tool justification remains in the parent version; this claim accounts only for the two-tool increase to 464.

registry.packFiles.reason: BI-012487AA: document-family-tools.ts holds the four render-family tool definitions and their one shared handler, composed into the existing document pack (the provider-account-tools.ts pattern), so document-pack.ts does not grow toward the module ceiling. Not a second registration path: document-pack.test.ts proves each tool is registered once with grants equal to the single source in document-tool-grants.ts. BI-1914A351: provider-account-tools.ts holds the two account tool definitions composed into the existing model-provider pack. Handlers remain in that pack and delegate to shared account services, avoiding a larger import cycle. This is an account contract module, not a second tool registration path. Claim to check: model-provider pack tests prove one registration and matching grants for each account control. BI-B8437D03 extracts the existing five nonproduction lease definitions into nonprod-lease-definitions.ts, composed once by the existing nonprod-lease pack. This keeps timing validation and handlers below the module ceiling without adding a tool, core-tier entry, grant or registration path. Claim to check: existing pack tests retain the same five names, grants and handlers, with requestedTtlMs constrained to an integer; tool-definition and dispatch baselines remain unchanged. BI-A009189A: work-thread-feedback.ts is one thin definition/handler contract module composed once into the existing work-thread pack. It separates exact-answer feedback from delegation and keeps the pack below its module limit; it creates no second pack, registration path or handler authority. Shared THREAD_TOOL_GRANTS and pack tests prove one registration, matching grants and preserved delegation behavior.

tier.coreToolNames.reason: Adds the five names without which a core-tier client can start governed work but never finish it: update_backlog_item_status and record_execution_evidence (AGENTS.md s5 requires recording completion and its evidence, and core could create/triage/size/update but not close); trace_code_surface (a surface's implementation files and tests, pairing with search_code_graph which is already core); and claim_nonprod_environment_lease with release_nonprod_environment_lease together, since a session that can take the shared singleton lock but not release it blocks every other worktree and the CI gate. A client that cannot close its own work reaches for ?tier=full and pays the whole ~400-tool surface to recover two names. No effect on Claude Code or Codex, whose client-aware default is already full. Raise again only for a tool without which governed work cannot be finished; convenience stays behind search_tool_marketplace.
